about: The rpc and log --json fields a client may rely on (ADR 0048 section 6, ADR 0025 sections 4 and 5), held by tests in tests/modes.rs. An event's fields are under its "fields" object, beside "message": those always present, those present only in the case a list is named for (a turn that called the model, a blast_radius turn, a prompt-sending driver, a response header the endpoint sent), and, under "absent_when", when a listed field is still left off. A figure trellis did not measure is absent, never 0. A response's data, per command, is under "responses": the fields always in it, and those present only for one value of another; get_codebase's and get_queue's are dotted paths, with [] meaning each element of an array (#559). A response's id is the id its command was sent with, and a run's run_start and run_end carry the id of the prompt that started it. Fields not listed here are unversioned.

absent_when.model_ms: the governance audit's turn event, which makes no model call (trellis-loop agent.rs ~909-919)
absent_when.prompt_bytes: the governance audit's turn event, which sends no prompt
absent_when.completion_tokens: the governance audit's turn event, which reads no reply; or a reply the step read reported no output tokens (the provider stub's replies all report them)
absent_when.queue_wait_ms: a reply the step read carried no x-colibri-queue-wait-ms header

optional.restored: when the outcome is not_converged or interrupted

optional.data: when success is true and the command answers with data

null_when.configured: neither the repository's config nor the user's sets [model] spec
null_when.probed[].error: the runtime answered; local then holds the specs it listed that first_run would offer
null_when.providers[].key_variable: the provider's protocol is not one trellis knows

list_models.about: local holds vllm:http://<address>#<model> specs, each one first_run would offer; probed names every address tried, in first_run's order (Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM on their default ports); providers are the user config's [[providers]], by name and the variable a key would be read from, never its value (#564)

null_when.saved_to: save was not asked for, or the model is the configured one confirmed

set_model.about: {model, save?} names this session's model, and with save true writes it to the user's config file, never .trellis/config.toml; {configured: true} confirms the configured spec. Until one has succeeded, prompt is refused with an error that starts "choose a model first" (#564)

get_codebase.path: the module's file, relative to the root and /-separated
get_codebase.refused_when: the root has no .git entry (a directory, or the file a worktree or submodule has): success is false, the error names the command, the root and the rule, and nothing under the root is read

null_when.tasks[].assignee: the task names no agent profile
null_when.tasks[].waiting: the task is not pending, or nothing holds it back

empty_when.tasks[].blockers: the task waits on no other task

data.last_run: the last run's run_end framing fields, without type

null_when.run_request_id: no run is in flight, or the one in flight was started by a command sent with no id
null_when.model: neither set_model nor the configuration's [model] spec names one
null_when.last_run: no run of this rpc process has ended
null_when.tier: no run of this rpc process has decided its tier yet, or the last run stopped before deciding one; never guessed from the spec

tier_label.shape: <head>, or <head><detail_separator><detail>. A digit head is the adapter tier; unknown means nothing has established one; scripted means no model is called. <detail> is prose for a person (e.g. "native tool calls", "no schema", "unavailable: colibri olmoe refuses tools"), not a further format. A label never begins with the word tier: a status bar writes `tier ` before it.

overview.about: `trellis [--root <repo>] --json overview` prints one object (ADR 0050 section 3, ADR 0025 section 4, both amended 2026-10-07; #558), held by client_contract_overview_lists_what_the_overview_object_carries in tests/cli.rs. Outside a repository, or with a root that has no .git entry, it carries only the keys under outside_a_repository. A last_run, in recent or at the top, is null when there is no trail, {"error": <why>} when the newest trail will not parse, and otherwise the fields below. codebase is null when the cache is missing or stale, codebase_reason saying which (null when current). pr_ci.available false carries reason in place of pull_requests and runs. Strings from trails, the queue and gh are data written by others.

optional.recent_error: when the recent list cannot be read; recent is then empty
optional.last_run.error: in place of the other last_run fields, when the newest trail will not parse
optional.board.tasks_error: when the queue cannot be read; tasks is then null
